# NVDA — Quantitative Fundamental-Attractiveness Report
**Decision date: 2026-07-06**

---

## 1. Revenue, Earnings & Operating Trajectory

NVDA's Q1 FY2027 (period_end 2026-04-26) delivered **revenue of $81.61B** and **EPS of $2.39**, representing QoQ revenue growth of +43.2% and YoY revenue growth of +85.2%. EPS grew even faster: QoQ +83.8%, YoY +214.5%. The quarterly revenue sequence ($44.06B → $46.74B → $57.01B → $81.61B) shows compounding acceleration rather than linear growth. Gross profit surged QoQ +46.1% and YoY +129.3%, while operating cash flow exploded QoQ +112.0% ($23.75B → $50.34B). Net income in Q1 FY2027 was $58.32B, up +82.8% QoQ and +210.6% YoY.

**Margin expansion is the defining feature.** Gross margin expanded from 60.6% (Q1 FY2025: $26.67B / $44.06B) to 74.9% (Q1 FY2027: $61.16B / $81.61B) — a 1,430 bp shift. Operating margin widened from 49.1% to 65.6% over the same span. The latest ratios panel confirms trailing net margin at 0.63 (63%) versus 0.517 a year earlier, a 1,130 bp improvement. This is not just top-line leverage; cost discipline is demonstrably improving alongside revenue scale.

**Cash generation** is extraordinary in absolute terms: $50.34B of operating cash flow in a single quarter. The prior three quarters averaged $22.18B, indicating the Q1 FY2027 figure reflects genuine acceleration, not merely seasonality. Free cash flow data is unavailable (n/a); operating cash flow is used as the proxy for cash-generation assessment.

## 2. Earnings Quality & Balance-Sheet Resilience

Earnings quality is supported by **operating cash flow exceeding reported net income** ($50.34B OCF vs. $58.32B NI — the gap likely reflects timing of advance payments and working capital; both figures are massive). The three-quarter average OCF ($22.18B) against the three-quarter average net income ($25.70B) also shows healthy cash conversion.

The balance sheet is a **fortress**: total equity of $195.47B against total debt of $8.47B yields a **debt-to-equity of 0.043x**. Total assets grew from $125.25B (Q1 FY2025) to $259.47B — more than doubling — entirely through retained earnings and operating expansion, not leverage. Total liabilities ($64.00B) are modest relative to assets ($259.47B). The equity base expanded by $111.63B over the four-quarter lookback, reflecting the magnitude of retained earnings. There is no balance-sheet risk to flag.

**ROE is exceptionally high at 0.817 (81.7%)**, down modestly from 0.916 a year earlier. The decline reflects the expanding equity denominator outpacing net income growth on a rolling basis; this is a sign of financial strength accumulating, not deterioration.

## 3. Valuation Versus Own History (Ratios)

This is where the analysis becomes most interesting. The PE (diluted) stands at **29.8x** as of 2026-07-02 — at the **absolute floor of its 365-day window** (range: 29.4x–66.8x). One year ago (2025-07-07), the PE was 50.7x. The valuation has compressed by 41% while earnings have more than tripled. This is not a "cheap" multiple in absolute terms, but relative to the earnings trajectory, the market is paying **less per unit of earnings power than at any point in the observed history**.

P/B has similarly compressed from 46.4x (2025-07-07) to **24.3x**, near the window floor of 24.0x. P/S stands at 18.7x.

**Earnings yield at 3.4%** now meaningfully closes the gap with the 10-year Treasury yield (4.49%), yielding a spread of only ~109 bp. A year ago, with PE at 50.7x (earnings yield ~2.0%) and the 10-year near similar levels, the gap was much wider. The improved earnings yield makes the equity compensation for risk more defensible, though it is still below the risk-free rate — meaning forward growth expectations must deliver for the valuation to work.

**Crucially: this PE compression occurred because earnings grew faster than the stock price, not because the market lost faith.** The stock is essentially flat over 12 months while EPS grew +214.5% YoY. The multiple decline is arithmetic re-rating toward earnings power — a healthy dynamic.

## 4. Price Context

Price closed at **$194.83 on 2026-07-02**, within a 52-week range of $157.34–$236.54. The quarterly path shows volatility: Q2 (Dec–Apr) saw a −6.3% drawdown, Q3 (Apr–Jul) recovered +10.9%. The stock remains ~18% below its 52-week high. Price has not kept pace with the fundamental acceleration — it is the fundamental strength that is making the valuation compelling, not a price selloff.

## 5. Macro & Sentiment Overlays

**Macro** is benign for this business. The Fed funds rate (3.63%) is stable and modestly accommodative. The VIX (15.81) is well below its 90-day peak of 25.78, indicating normalized risk appetite. Oil has collapsed from $114.58 (Apr) to $69.73 — reducing input-cost risk and broader inflationary pressure. The yield curve (10Y-2Y spread at 0.35%) remains positive but flattening, suggesting no imminent recession signal. Rising long-end rates (10Y at 4.49%, up from ~4.26 in mid-April) modestly pressure growth multiples, but the PE compression already discounts this.

**Sentiment** is moderately positive (90-day mean score = 0.44, n=1,678 articles). No extreme readings — neither euphoria nor panic. This is a neutral to mildly supportive overlay. Recent daily scores show no clear trend. Sentiment does not drive the thesis.

## 6. Strongest Quantitative Upside and Downside

**Upside:** (1) If the current Q1 FY2027 revenue run rate sustains even partially, forward earnings power implies a PE well below 20x on a forward basis — the market may be under-appreciating durability. (2) Margins at 74.9% gross / 65.6% operating, if sustained, represent a structural step-change in profitability that prior-cycle PE multiples (50x+) implicitly did not price for. (3) A PE of 29.8x with a near-4% earnings yield at the bottom of its historical range leaves re-rating room if growth persists.

**Downside:** (1) The revenue trajectory ($44B → $82B in four quarters) is historically extreme and may reflect pulled-forward AI capex spending that normalizes. (2) The 3.4% earnings yield still trails the 4.49% risk-free rate — if growth decelerates, the multiple has room to compress further. (3) Gross margin at 74.9% is historically unprecedented; any reversion toward the ~60% level seen in Q1 FY2025 would materially impair earnings. (4) TTM data is unavailable due to fiscal-quarter reporting gaps (incomplete fiscal year), preventing a full trailing-twelve-month validation.

## 7. Provisional Quantitative Conclusion

NVDA presents a compelling fundamental case: revenue and earnings are accelerating at exceptional rates, margins have structurally expanded by 1,000+ bp, cash generation is massive, and the balance sheet carries virtually no leverage (D/E 0.043x). The PE at 29.8x — the floor of its 365-day range — represents the cheapest valuation relative to actual demonstrated earnings power in the observed window. This is not a value trap; it is earnings outrunning price.

The primary risk is durability: the growth trajectory is historically extraordinary and may not be sustainable. The earnings yield (3.4%) still falls below the 10-year Treasury (4.49%), meaning the market still requires continued growth to justify the multiple. If the AI infrastructure cycle persists, the current valuation offers significant upside from both earnings growth and potential re-rating. If it normalizes, the multiple has room to compress further.

**Quantitative attractiveness: Favorable.** The fundamentals-to-valuation relationship is the most attractive it has been across the entire observed window, driven by genuine earnings power expansion rather than price dislocation.

# NVDA — Qualitative Franchise & Risk Assessment

**Decision date: 2026-07-06 | Report date: 2026-07-06**

---

## 1. Business / Franchise Read

Nvidia designs GPUs and, increasingly, full AI compute systems (GPUs, networking, software) sold to hyperscalers, AI cloud providers, enterprises, and sovereign AI initiatives. As of Q1 FY2027 (reported 2026-05-20), data center revenue dominates the franchise. In Q1, total revenue was $81.6B (+85% YoY) with data center as the clear engine; the company recently re-segmented into **Data Center** (broken into Hyperscale and AI Clouds, Industrial & Enterprise) and **Edge Computing** (gaming, professional visualization, auto, OEM) to better expose its growth drivers.

**Structural moat:** The CUDA software ecosystem creates high switching costs for developers and hyperscalers. Nvidia holds roughly 94–95% share of AI training GPUs and 74% of AI inference chips (per news citing market data). Its networking business nearly tripled YoY in Q1, expanding the systems-level revenue capture beyond discrete GPU sales. Gross margins run ~75%, and the company generated ~$48.5B in quarterly operating cash flow (structural web_search). The franchise is a platform, not a commodity chip vendor — hardware, networking, and software sold as an integrated stack.

**Capital allocation philosophy** is aggressive but rational: a $25B bond issuance (30-year maturities, ~4.25–5.6% cost) drew $85B in demand, reflecting AA credit. The company simultaneously authorized $80B in share buybacks and raised its dividend 25x to $0.25/share quarterly. Supply-related commitments to TSMC and partners total $119B as of Q1, signaling confidence in multi-year demand. Strategic investments (~$18B+ portfolio) span CoreWeave, Intel, Nokia, Corning, Synopsys, and others — an ecosystem-building strategy, not passive capital deployment.

**Structural growth:** Wall Street consensus projects ~82% revenue growth for FY2027 (~$392B) and ~88% EPS growth. The Vera Rubin architecture, expected to ship H2 FY2027, promises 10x reduction in inference costs and 4x in training costs, with 25% higher system pricing. Data center industry projections remain robust: $1T+ in hyperscaler capex for 2027, and the data center infrastructure market projected to grow at 10.9% CAGR to $752B by 2034.

## 2. Recent Developments (News + Updates)

**Stock performance and valuation (July 2026):** NVDA has underperformed in 2026 — up only ~5–7% YTD versus AMD (+171%) and Intel (+278%) in H1. The stock declined ~13% from its May all-time high of ~$236, falling below $5T market cap. However, at 21–22x forward earnings, it now trades below Coca-Cola's P/E and near its cheapest multiple in 7 years (7-year average ~71x). Multiple Motley Fool analysts identify it as undervalued given growth projections.

**Earnings beat (2026-05-20):** Q1 FY2027 EPS of $1.87 beat consensus $1.70; revenue of $81.6B beat $79.19B consensus. Q2 guidance points to ~$91B revenue.

**CPU market entry:** Nvidia is launching CPUs targeting the ~$200B data center CPU market, with Vera Rubin CPU platform expected H2 2026. This is a material TAM expansion beyond GPU dominance.

**Competitive dynamics (June–July 2026):** Google and Amazon are pushing custom TPUs and Trainium chips via financing incentives to reduce Nvidia dependency. Broadcom's custom ASIC business is growing aggressively ($20B → projected $100B by FY2027). Amazon is in early talks to sell Trainium externally. However, analysts note Nvidia's CUDA ecosystem and 95%+ GPU market share remain formidable barriers.

**Export controls (June 2026):** The U.S. Department of Commerce closed a loophole allowing Rubin and Blackwell chips to reach China through offshore subsidiaries. Analysts estimate a cumulative China revenue headwind of $5.5B–$16B. The Q2 guide of $91B already assumes zero data center sales to China.

**Palantir partnership (2026-06-29):** Expanded strategic collaboration to build sovereign AI solutions for U.S. government agencies, combining Nvidia's Nemotron models with Palantir's infrastructure.

**Regulatory overhang:** Taiwan investigation into chip smuggling (~$160M in diverted H100/H200 chips); Senator Warren demanded export compliance explanations by June 18, 2026.

**Market rotation:** July 1 saw a 4.4% semiconductor sector selloff while non-AI sectors rallied; Meta's cloud business announcement pressured neocloud stocks. Rotation from mega-cap AI beneficiaries toward value/industrials is underway.

## 3. Material Risks & Offsets

| Risk | Evidence | Offset |
|------|----------|--------|
| **AI capex cycle peak / ROI doubt** | Hyperscalers spending $700B+ annually; investors demanding proof of cash conversion. Mag-7 basket is splitting as cash-flow scrutiny intensifies (2026-06-26 Investing.com). | Signed $119B supply commitments; $1T+ hyperscaler capex guided for 2027. Q1 beat + Q2 guide of $91B show no demand deceleration. |
| **Custom silicon competition** | Google TPU circular financing, Amazon Trainium external sales, Broadcom ASIC growth to $100B. 65% of revenue from 4 customers who are developing alternatives (SeekingAlpha bear case). | CUDA switching costs; 94% GPU share; networking revenue tripling shows systems-level lock-in. Vera Rubin cost advantages maintain lead. |
| **China export controls** | Loophole closed June 2026; cumulative $5.5–$16B revenue headwind. Zero China DC revenue in current guidance. | Already fully absorbed into forward guidance. Non-China demand growing fast enough to compensate. |
| **Margin compression** | Memory chip costs rising (Micron 84% gross margin); B200 compute pricing falling; GPU rental prices declining. | Vera Rubin priced 25% above Blackwell; integrated systems capture more value per dollar of capex. 75% gross margins sustained. |
| **Valuation re-rating risk** | Stock at 21–22x forward after multiple compression from 34x historical average. | This is the opportunity, not the risk — multiple is at 7-year lows despite accelerating earnings. If Vera Rubin cycle delivers, re-rating to 30–40x is plausible. |
| **Concentration / execution** | $119B supply commitments are massive forward bets; Vera Rubin production ramp risk (early Blackwell delays in 2024–25). | $48.5B quarterly operating cash flow; AA credit; $80B buyback room provides cushion. |

## 4. Qualitative Assessment

**Positive.** Nvidia possesses a rare combination: an entrenched, ecosystem-driven franchise in the highest-growth segment of global technology, generating extraordinary cash flow at scale, with a credible next product cycle (Vera Rubin) and a credible TAM expansion (CPUs). The structural narrative is intact — CUDA moat, systems-level selling, accelerating networking revenue, and $119B in forward supply commitments signal durable demand. The stock's pullback to ~22x forward earnings — near S&P 500 average — against 82–88% projected growth creates a qualitatively attractive entry relative to franchise quality. Risks are real (China headwinds, custom chip competition, capex cycle uncertainty) but are largely priced in and partially absorbed. The balance of evidence favors fundamental attractiveness: this is a category-defining franchise in a structural growth cycle, temporarily compressed by sentiment headwinds and sector rotation, not by franchise deterioration.
